content.comment_body: Hello, For a project needing to manage 80 fan coil units with customized graphics and time scheduling via a touch panel, we are considering using [product_name] + [product_name]. Is it possible to use multiple [product_name] modules with a single [product_name] and [product_name] panel? Many Thanks,

Hi, Yes, it's feasible to use more than one [product_name] with a single [product_name]. However, only one module configuration is officially tested by [company_name]. If you utilize the [product_name] VM-Memory, please note it only supports 850 Bytes, which can be a limiting factor especially if integrated in your project logic. Hope this helps

Hello, Thank you for your previous advice. Considering the VM-memory limitation, is it possible to use two separate setups, each with one [product_name] and one [product_name], then connect both to a single [product_name] panel? Thanks,
Yes, you can connect two [product_name] devices to one [product_name] HMI panel.
Hello! Thank you for your advice.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are investigating how to scale a fan coil unit control system by integrating multiple [product_name] communication modules and base modules with an HMI panel. Key user concerns are related to memory limitations in the [product_name] device and the fact that only some setups have been officially validated by [company_name]. Users are seeking solutions for overcoming device resource constraints and maintaining reliable compatibility between components.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate scaling control by adding multiple communication modules, while keeping the system stable and compatible with the HMI panel. They expect clear information about configuration limitations and recommendations for supported setups.
